newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Anheuser sees modest market share rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Anheuser sees modest market share rise.

text.p: Beer brewer Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc, whose leading U.S. beer market share was flat for the first six months of the year, said it expected to show a slight increase in market share for all of 1997.

"We expect to have a modest share increase for the year," W. Randolph "Randy" Baker, chief financial officer, said in a telephone interview on Wednesday. "We are seeing some improvements in sales trends now that we are positioned competitively."
Anheuser, whose beer brands include Budweiser and Bud Light, ended 1996 with a 45.2 percent market share.

For the first six months of 1997, Anheuser's market share was 44.3 percent, essentially flat with the year-ago period. Company officials said market share varies between quarters and comparisons are made between comparable periods.
Earlier, Anheuser said its second quarter worldwide beer volume rose 0.8 percent to 25.6 million barrels, including a 0.8 percent increase in the United States to 23.8 million barrels.
Baker said domestic sales gains were hampered by competitive pricing and promotions in the United States.
"There is wide spread promotional discounting activity," he added.
But he said he does not believe it is a "sustainable strategy" for Anheuser's competitors, particularly in the premium-priced brands.

Matching competitive pricing in the short-term has put a lid on its earnings gains for the year. Anheuser said earnings per share growth for all of 1997 likely will be in line with the 8.5 percent increase posted in the first half.
But Anheuser's long-term growth objective remains for a double-digit increase in earnings per share.
"We reaffirmed our long-term objective," Baker said. "We believe that the activities in the market place are of a short-term nature...We don't believe it's sustainable."
